title: Weak association is preserved and reflected by etale algebra maps
statement: Let $A\to B$ be a homomorphism of commutative rings such that $\operatorname{Spec}B\to\operatorname{Spec}A$ is etale [def-weil-etale-morphism]. Let $L$ be any $A$-module, let $\mathfrak b\subset B$ be a prime ideal, and let $\mathfrak a$ be its inverse image in $A$. For a ring $T$ and a $T$-module $P$, define $\operatorname{WeakAss}_T(P)$ to consist of primes minimal among those containing $\operatorname{Ann}_T(x)=\{t\in T:tx=0\}$ for some $x\in P$. Give $L\otimes_A B$ the $B$-action on the second factor [def-weil-pbc-module-tensor-product]. Then $\mathfrak b\in\operatorname{WeakAss}_B(L\otimes_A B)$ if and only if $\mathfrak a\in\operatorname{WeakAss}_A(L)$. No Noetherian or finite-generation assumption is imposed.

proof.text: For ascent, assume $\mathfrak a\in\operatorname{WeakAss}_A(L)$. Put $R=A_{\mathfrak a}$, $S=B_{\mathfrak b}$, $M=L_{\mathfrak a}$ and $N=L\otimes_A B$. By [lem-sc-weakass-localization], there is $x\in M$ with $\sqrt{I}=\mathfrak aR$, where $I=\operatorname{Ann}_R(x)$. The etale hypothesis [def-weil-etale-morphism] gives flatness of the spectrum morphism; [lem-weil-pbc-flat-ring-map-iff-flat-affine] gives flatness of $A\to B$, and [lem-weil-pbc-flat-local-ring-maps] gives flatness of the induced local map $R\to S$. All these statements allow arbitrary rings; neither $L$ nor its localization is assumed finite.

source.place: Tag 05F0, lemma-weakly-ass-pullback, proof, first two sentences; Tag 0566, lemma-weakly-ass-local

proof.text: The map $R/I\to M$, $[r]\mapsto rx$, is injective by the definition of $I$. Flatness [def-weil-pbc-flat-ring-map] therefore makes $(R/I)\otimes_R S\to M\otimes_R S$ injective. The tensor definition identifies its source with $S/IS$: $[r]\otimes s\mapsto[rs]$, with inverse $[s]\mapsto[1]\otimes s$. The relations on both sides verify these maps are well defined and inverse. If $y=x\otimes1$, injectivity gives $\operatorname{Ann}_S(y)=IS$. Also $M\otimes_R S\cong N_{\mathfrak b}$: the map $(l/u)\otimes(b/v)\mapsto(l\otimes b)/(\varphi(u)v)$ has inverse $(l\otimes b)/v\mapsto(l/1)\otimes(b/v)$, extended additively. The fraction relations and tensor balancing verify the two inverse formulas. Here $u\notin\mathfrak a$, $v\notin\mathfrak b$, so every displayed denominator is invertible.

source.place: Tag 05F0, lemma-weakly-ass-pullback, proof: the annihilator after tensoring; fraction and quotient identifications written out

proof.text: By [lem-weil-pbc-etale-prime-generates-maximal], $(\mathfrak aR)S=\mathfrak bS$. Thus $IS\subseteq\mathfrak bS$. For $z\in\mathfrak bS$, write $z=\sum_{i=1}^k s_i a_i$ with $a_i\in\mathfrak aR$. Since $\sqrt I=\mathfrak aR$, choose $e_i\ge1$ with $a_i^{e_i}\in I$. Every term in the expansion of $z^{1+\sum_i(e_i-1)}$ contains some $a_i^{e_i}$, so this power lies in $IS$ (and $z=0$ is immediate). Hence $\sqrt{IS}=\mathfrak bS$. The element $y$ of step 2 is therefore a radical-annihilator witness in $N_{\mathfrak b}$, and [lem-sc-weakass-localization] gives $\mathfrak b\in\operatorname{WeakAss}_B(N)$. This proves ascent without a finite-generation assumption.

source.place: Tag 05F0, lemma-weakly-ass-pullback, proof, last sentences; for etale maps the fibre maximal ideal is zero, Tag 00U4

proof.text:
For descent, assume $\mathfrak b\in\operatorname{WeakAss}_B(N)$. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-etale-locally-standard] to choose $g
otin\mathfrak b$ and an $A$-algebra isomorphism $B_g\cong C_h$, where $C=A[t]/(f)$ and $f$ is monic. Let $\mathfrak b_g$ be the prime in $B_g$ consisting of fractions whose numerator lies in $\mathfrak b$. This is well defined and prime because $g
otin\mathfrak b$; its inverse image in $B$ is $\mathfrak b$. Transport it to a prime of $C_h$ and contract to $\mathfrak r\subset C$. Then $h
otin\mathfrak r$, its extension is the transported prime (a fraction belongs exactly when its numerator does), and $\mathfrak r\cap A=\mathfrak a$. By [lem-weil-pbc-monic-quotient-free], $C$ is a finite free $A$-module with power basis $e_1,\ldots,e_n$. The existence of $\mathfrak r$ rules out $n=0$, for the monic degree-zero polynomial is $1$ and its quotient is the zero ring.

source.place: Tag 05FP, lemma-etale-weak-assassin-up-down, proof: standard etale chart and the finite free algebra A[t]/(f)

proof.text: Put $K=L\otimes_A C$. Localization at the displayed primes gives $B_{\mathfrak b}\cong(B_g)_{\mathfrak b_g}\cong(C_h)_{\mathfrak rC_h}\cong C_{\mathfrak r}$. These identifications follow directly from fractions: if $s$ is outside a prime, inverting $s$ and then all elements outside the extended prime is the same as inverting all elements outside the original prime, with $(a/s^i)/(b/s^j)\mapsto as^j/(bs^i)$. Tensoring with $L$ has the analogous explicit identification $(l\otimes c)/v\leftrightarrow l\otimes(c/v)$; its inverse and balancing follow from the same fraction relation. Thus $N_{\mathfrak b}\cong K_{\mathfrak r}$, compatibly with the local ring isomorphism and their maximal ideals. By [lem-sc-weakass-localization] applied first to $(B,N,\mathfrak b)$ and then to $(C,K,\mathfrak r)$, the assumed weak association at $\mathfrak b$ gives weak association at $\mathfrak r$: the radical-annihilator witness in the first localized module maps to one in the second, and the converse localization criterion returns $\mathfrak r\in\operatorname{WeakAss}_C(K)$.

source.place: Tag 05FP, lemma-etale-weak-assassin-up-down, reduction to the finite free algebra; Tag 0566, lemma-weakly-ass-local, provides the localization criterion

proof.text: The map $A\to C$ is finite by step 4. Apply [lem-trf-finite-ring-map-weakass-contraction] to the arbitrary $C$-module $K$ and its weakly associated prime $\mathfrak r$. Its contraction is $\mathfrak a$, so $\mathfrak a\in\operatorname{WeakAss}_A(K)$, where $K$ now denotes the module with its restricted $A$-action. This step uses finiteness of $C$ over $A$, not finiteness of $K$ over either ring.

source.place: Tag 05E1, lemma-weakly-ass-finite-ring-map; this is the finite-pushforward step of Tag 05FN

proof.text: The basis from step 4 identifies $K$ with $L^n$: $l\otimes\sum_i a_i e_i\mapsto(a_i l)_i$, with inverse $(l_i)_i\mapsto\sum_i l_i\otimes e_i$. The tensor relations verify these are inverse $A$-linear maps. Choose a witness $(l_1,\ldots,l_n)$ for step 6, and set $I_i=\operatorname{Ann}_A(l_i)$. Its annihilator is $J=\bigcap_i I_i$, and $\mathfrak a$ is minimal over $J$. Since $\prod_i I_i\subseteq J\subseteq\mathfrak a$ and $\mathfrak a$ is prime, some $I_j\subseteq\mathfrak a$: otherwise choose $a_i\in I_i\setminus\mathfrak a$ and their product contradicts primality. Any prime $\mathfrak p$ with $I_j\subseteq\mathfrak p\subseteq\mathfrak a$ contains $J$, so minimality over $J$ forces $\mathfrak p=\mathfrak a$. Thus $\mathfrak a$ is minimal over $\operatorname{Ann}_A(l_j)$, proving $\mathfrak a\in\operatorname{WeakAss}_A(L)$. Together with step 3 this proves both directions.

source.place: Tag 05FN, lemma-finite-flat-weak-assassin-up-down, proof: weak association of a positive finite direct sum; the annihilator argument is expanded here
